## Overview

mgcvUI is an interactive Shiny application for building Generalized
Additive Models (GAMs) via the `mgcv` package. It is designed for real
estate appraisers who need transparent, defensible nonlinear models, but
is useful for anyone doing regression modeling with smooth terms.

mgcvUI can run **standalone** (import a CSV/Excel file, configure smooths,
fit a GAM, generate a report) or as part of a **two-stage pipeline** with
earthUI, where MARS models discover breakpoints and mgcvUI refines them
into smooth, statistically rigorous curves.

## Application Layout

The sidebar contains numbered workflow steps:

1. **Import Data** -- Browse for a CSV or Excel file (read directly from
   disk, no upload size limits).
2. **Import from earthUI** (optional) -- Browse for an earthUI result
   `.rds` file to seed knot positions from a MARS model.
3. **Variable Configuration** -- Select the response variable, configure
   predictors (include/exclude, type, special roles, factor/linear flags).
4. **Predictor Settings** -- The variable table showing all columns with
   checkboxes for Inc, Factor, Linear, and dropdowns for Type and Special.
5. **Mgcv Call Parameters** -- Family, method, gamma, select, basis, k,
   and advanced parameters (optimizer, scale, discrete, threads).
6. **Fit Mgcv GAM Model** -- Click to fit.
7. **Download** -- Export estimated prices, residuals, and reports.

The main panel shows results in tabs: Data, Equation, Summary, Variable
Importance, Contribution (smooth plots), Correlation, Diagnostics,
RCA Adjustments, Anova, Mgcv Output, Sign Check, Concurvity, and Basis Check.

## Parameter Presets

mgcvUI provides two parameter presets, selectable at the top of the
Mgcv Call Parameters section:

### Standalone (Discovery)

Use when fitting a GAM without earth knot input. mgcv must discover the
nonlinearities itself.

| Setting | Value | Reason |
|---------|-------|--------|
| Default basis | `tp` (thin plate) | Adaptive; finds shape without pre-specified knots |
| Default k | 0 (auto = 10) | Needs flexibility to discover nonlinearity |
| Gamma | 1.2 | Mild parsimony bias |
| Select | TRUE | Lets mgcv drop unhelpful terms |
| Method | REML | Best for correlated predictors, small n |

### Earth Pipeline (Refinement)

Auto-selected when an earthUI result is imported. Earth already found the
breakpoints; mgcv's job is regularized estimation, not discovery.

| Setting | Value | Reason |
|---------|-------|--------|
| Default basis | `cr` (cubic regression) | Faster, interpretable, uses earth knot positions directly |
| Default k | 5 | Earth already found breakpoints; low k prevents refitting |
| Gamma | 1.4 | Stronger parsimony bias (Wood & Fasiolo recommendation) |
| Select | TRUE | Second-stage shrinkage guard |
| Method | REML | Best for correlated predictors, small n |

All values remain individually editable after a preset is applied.

## Mgcv Call Parameters Reference

### Core Parameters

| Parameter | UI Control | Default | Description |
|-----------|-----------|---------|-------------|
| **Family** | Dropdown | gaussian | Distribution family. Use `gaussian` for continuous sale prices, `Gamma` for strictly positive values |
| **Method** | Dropdown | REML | Smoothing parameter estimation method. REML is strongly preferred over GCV.Cp for correlated predictors and modest sample sizes |
| **Gamma** | Numeric | 1.2 / 1.4 | Inflates the effective degrees of freedom penalty. Values > 1 bias toward smoother fits. 1.4 is the Wood recommendation for parsimony |
| **CV** | Checkbox | TRUE | 10-fold cross-validated R-squared |
| **Select** | Checkbox | TRUE | Adds a shrinkage penalty so smooth terms can be penalized to zero. This is the `select` argument to `mgcv::gam()` |
| **Default basis** | Dropdown | tp / cr | Basis type for smooth terms. `tp` = thin plate regression spline (adaptive), `cr` = cubic regression spline (fast, interpretable) |
| **Default k** | Numeric | 0 / 5 | Basis dimension (max wiggliness). 0 = auto (mgcv default of 10). Lower values produce smoother curves |
| **Tensor type** | Dropdown | ti | `ti` = tensor interaction (recommended), `te` = tensor product |

### Advanced Parameters

These are under the "Advanced Parameters" collapsible and rarely need changing:

| Parameter | Default | When to Change |
|-----------|---------|----------------|
| **Optimizer** | outer/newton | Switch to `outer/bfgs` if newton convergence fails. `efs` for very large models |
| **Scale** | 0 (estimate) | Fix to a known value for quasi-families or known-variance situations |
| **Discrete** | FALSE | Enable for large datasets (>10k rows) for faster fitting via covariate discretization |
| **Threads** | 1 | Increase for parallel computation on multi-core machines (e.g., 4-8 on Apple Silicon) |

## Predictor Settings

The variable table shows one row per column in your data (excluding the
response). Each row has:

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **Variable** | Column name |
| **Type** | Detected data type (numeric, integer, character, factor, etc.) |
| **Inc** | Include in the model |
| **Special** | Column role: `no` (default), `actual_age`, `area`, `concessions`, `contract_date`, `display_only`, `dom`, `effective_age`, `latitude`, `listing_date`, `living_area`, `longitude`, `lot_size`, `sale_age`, `site_dimensions`, `weights` |
| **Factor** | Treat as a factor (categorical) variable |
| **Linear** | Force linear (no smooth) |
| **NAs** | Count and percentage of missing values |

Variables with > 50% NAs are automatically excluded. Variables with only 2
unique values are automatically converted to factors.

## Interactions

### Tensor Interactions (continuous x continuous)

The Allowed Interactions matrix shows all included smooth (non-linear,
non-factor) predictors. Check a cell to add a tensor interaction term
(`ti(var1, var2)` or `te(var1, var2)`) to the model.

When earth knots are imported, interactions detected by earth or allowed
by the earthUI allowed matrix are pre-checked.

### Factor-by-Smooth Interactions (factor x continuous)

Below the tensor matrix, the Factor-by-Smooth section shows a grid of
included factor variables (columns) vs. included smooth variables (rows).

Checking a cell generates `s(smooth_var, by=factor_var)` -- this fits a
**separate smooth curve for each level** of the factor. For example,
`s(lot_size, by=area_id)` lets the lot size effect vary by neighborhood.

The factor variable's main effect is already in the model as a linear
term (needed for level-specific intercepts).

### Block from Main Effect (Interaction Only)

**Right-click** a variable name in the Allowed Interactions matrix to
block it from entering the model as a main smooth term. A bold **" 1"**
indicator appears after the variable name.

When blocked:

- The variable gets **no** main `s()` smooth term
- The variable **can still** appear in tensor interactions
  (`ti(var1, var2)`) and factor-by-smooth interactions
  (`s(var, by=factor)`)
- Right-click again to unblock
- State persists via localStorage

**Use case:** When modeling time adjustments that should scale with
property size, block `sale_age` from the main effect and allow it only
in a tensor interaction with `living_area`. This generates
`ti(sale_age, living_area)` without a standalone `s(sale_age)` -- the
time appreciation rate varies smoothly with house size rather than being
a flat $/day rate.

This feature works identically across earthUI, glmnetUI, and mgcvUI.
In earthUI, it blocks degree-1 hinge functions. In glmnetUI, it removes
the variable from main formula terms. In mgcvUI, it removes the main
smooth term. In all three, the variable remains available for
interactions.

## What earthUI Imports Provide

When you import an earthUI result `.rds` file, mgcvUI extracts and uses
the following components:

| Component | Source in Earth Model | How mgcvUI Uses It |
|-----------|----------------------|---------------------|
| **Knot positions** | `model$cuts` + `model$selected.terms` | Placed as `cr` basis knots via `gam(..., knots=)`. Earth found the breakpoints; mgcv smooths through them |
| **Hinge directions** (signs) | `model$dirs` (+1 = forward, -1 = reverse) | Sign consistency check compares earth direction with GAM smooth derivative to flag contradictions |
| **Interactions** | Rows in `dirs` where 2+ predictors are nonzero | Pre-checks the Allowed Interactions matrix |
| **Target variable** | `earth_result$target` | Auto-sets the response dropdown |
| **Predictors** | `earth_result$predictors` | Auto-checks "Inc" for each predictor |
| **Categoricals** | `earth_result$categoricals` | Auto-checks "Factor" for categorical variables |
| **Linear predictors** | `earth_result$linpreds` | Auto-checks "Linear" for variables earth forced linear |
| **Interaction degree** | `earth_result$degree` | Shows info message if degree=1 (no interactions) |
| **Allowed matrix** | `earth_result$allowed_matrix` | Seeds the interaction matrix checkboxes |
| **R-squared, GCV, n_terms** | `model$rsq`, `model$gcv`, `length(selected.terms)` | Displayed in the earth import summary panel |
| **Data** | `earth_result$data` | Available for reference but not directly used (user imports their own data file) |

The key insight: **earth's job is discovery, mgcv's job is regularized
estimation**. The knots are the bridge -- they tell mgcv *where* the
nonlinearities are so it doesn't have to find them itself.

## Concurvity

Concurvity is the smooth analog of multicollinearity. Earth's hinge
functions on correlated predictors (e.g., living area and room count) can
produce near-concurve smooth terms in mgcv.

The **Concurvity** tab (in the results panel) shows:

- **Overall Concurvity** -- `mgcv::concurvity(model, full=TRUE)` with
  three measures (worst, observed, estimate) for each smooth term.
- **Pairwise Concurvity** -- `mgcv::concurvity(model, full=FALSE)` showing
  the worst-case concurvity between each pair of smooth terms.

Cells are color-coded:

| Color | Value Range | Interpretation |
|-------|-------------|----------------|
| White | < 0.5 | No concern |
| Yellow | 0.5 -- 0.8 | Moderate; monitor |
| Red | > 0.8 | High; consider dropping or collapsing one of the terms |

Values above ~0.8 in the "worst" row warrant collapsing or dropping one
of the terms before treating the model as defensible.

## Results Tabs Reference

| Tab | Contents |
|-----|----------|
| **Data** | Preview of the imported data |
| **Equation** | LaTeX-rendered model equation with smooth function definitions |
| **Summary** | R-squared, CV R-squared, deviance explained, AIC, smooth and parametric term tables |
| **Variable Importance** | Bar chart and table ranked by F-statistic (smooth) or |t|-statistic (parametric) |
| **Contribution** | Interactive smooth plots (plotly) for each predictor showing partial effects with confidence bands |
| **Correlation** | Heatmap of pairwise correlations among numeric predictors |
| **Diagnostics** | Residual plots, Q-Q plot, and actual vs. predicted scatter |
| **RCA Adjustments** | Residual, net, and gross percentage adjustment plots |
| **Anova** | Combined parametric and smooth term ANOVA table |
| **Mgcv Output** | Raw `print(model)`, `summary(model)`, and overall concurvity |
| **Sign Check** | Earth vs. GAM direction consistency (only with earth import) |
| **Concurvity** | Overall and pairwise concurvity tables with color coding |
| **Basis Check** | `mgcv::gam.check()` output verifying basis dimension adequacy |

## Memory and Persistence

mgcvUI remembers your settings across sessions:

- **Locale** -- Country, paper size, and import locale are saved
  automatically to a SQLite database when changed.
- **Per-file settings** -- Response variable, predictor configuration,
  family, method, select, gamma are saved per data filename.
- **Last-used files** -- The data file and earth file paths are remembered;
  files are auto-loaded on next launch if they still exist at their
  original locations.

Settings are stored in `tools::R_user_dir("mgcvUI", "data")/settings.sqlite`.

## Memory Checks

Before loading any file, mgcvUI checks available system memory against the
file size (with an expansion multiplier: 3x for CSV, 5x for RDS). If
insufficient memory is detected, a clear error message is shown with the
file size, estimated memory needed, and available memory. This works on
macOS, Linux, and Windows.
